question.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y = \tan u, \qquad u = \sin x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = \sec^2 u,\qquad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm d x} = \cos x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡u\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
